programs.title_tr: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Toz Metal Kusuru & Yere İndirmeler
programs.title_en: Pratt & Whitney GTF (PW1100G) Powder Metal Defect & Groundings
programs.current_status_tr: Yüksek basınçlı türbin disklerindeki mikroskobik toz metal kirliliği nedeniyle küresel çapta yüzlerce A320neo/A321neo uçağı planlanmamış motor bakımına alındı. Ortalama motor revizyon süresi (TAT) 250-300 günü buluyor.
programs.current_status_en: Contaminated powder metal in high-pressure turbine disks required accelerated inspections; hundreds of A320neo family jets grounded globally with MRO shop turnaround times reaching 250-300 days.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY filosundaki yaklaşık 30-40 adet A320/A321neo uçağı yerde bekliyor; kapasite açığını kapatmak için ıslak kiralama (wet lease) ve mevcut A320ceo uçaklarının hizmet ömrünü uzatma yoluna gidildi. Pegasus filosu ağırlıklı CFM LEAP motorlu olduğu için doğrudan etkilenmedi.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Turkish Airlines has 30-40 A321neo aircraft parked; capacity shortfall managed via wet leases and extending older A320ceo service lives. Pegasus remains largely unaffected due to CFM LEAP engine selection.
programs.timeline_horizon: 2026 yılı boyunca ve 2027 ilk yarısına kadar sürmesi bekleniyor.
programs.source_reference: RTX Corporation / FAA Airworthiness Directives (AD 2024-0044) / THY KAP Açıklamaları

programs.title_tr: Boeing 737 MAX Üretim Kısıtı (FAA Aylık 38 Tavanı) & Tedarik Zinciri
programs.title_en: Boeing 737 MAX FAA Monthly 38 Cap & Supply Chain Bottlecks
programs.current_status_tr: FAA'in kalite ve montaj denetimleri kapsamında Boeing 737 üretimini aylık 38 uçak tavanında tutması ve Spirit AeroSystems gövde teslimat gecikmeleri nedeniyle 2026 teslimat takvimleri 3-6 ay geriye ötelendi. MAX 7 ve MAX 10 sertifikasyonu gecikmeye devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: FAA capped 737 production at 38/month pending quality audit milestones; Spirit AeroSystems fuselage supply constraints pushed airline delivery slots back by 3 to 6 months. MAX 7 and MAX 10 certification remains pending.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: SunExpress ve THY teslimatları planlanan takvimin gerisinde seyrediyor; havayolları yoğun yaz ve sonbahar kapasite planlamalarını mevcut gövdelerle optimize ediyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: SunExpress and Turkish Airlines delivery streams experiencing slot postponements; carriers optimizing utilization on existing fleet assets.
programs.timeline_horizon: Aylık 38 üretim tavanının 2026 sonuna kadar aşamalı olarak artırılması hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: FAA Oversight Directives / Boeing Quarterly Deliveries / Airline Fleet Filings

programs.title_tr: Airbus A321XLR Ticari Teslimatları & Dar Gövde Uzun Menzil Devrimi
programs.title_en: Airbus A321XLR Entry into Service & Long-Range Narrowbody Wave
programs.current_status_tr: EASA tip sertifikasyonunu tamamlayan A321XLR, Iberia tarafından Madrid-Boston hattında ilk ticari uçuşlarına başladı. 4.700 deniz mili (8.700 km) menziliyle dar gövdede transatlantik ve kıtalararası uçuş maliyetlerini %30 düşürüyor.
programs.current_status_en: Having achieved EASA certification, the A321XLR commenced transatlantic operations with launch customer Iberia. Its 4,700 nm range unlocks thin long-haul routes at 30% lower trip cost.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Orta Doğu, Afrika ve ikincil Avrupa şehirlerine doğrudan bağlantı potansiyeli nedeniyle bölge taşıyıcıları tarafından yakından izleniyor. THY ve Pegasus filo stratejilerinde uzun vadeli alternatif.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Closely monitored by regional carriers for secondary point-to-point routes into Africa, Central Asia and Europe; potential long-term fit for Istanbul network.
programs.source_reference: EASA Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS) / Airbus Commercial Aircraft Updates

programs.title_tr: Boeing 777-9 (777X) Test Uçuşları & Hizmete Giriş Tarihi
programs.current_status_tr: İtiş kolu bağlantı elemanındaki (thrust link) teknik arıza sonrası test uçuşları geçici olarak durdurulmuştu; Boeing ilk teslimat takvimini 2026 yılına (ve potansiyel olarak 2027'ye) revize etti. Başta Emirates ve Lufthansa olmak üzere amiral gemisi filoları A380 ve 777-300ER ömür uzatmak zorunda kaldı.
programs.current_status_en: Structural component inspection on engine thrust links required test fleet pause; initial deliveries rescheduled to 2026/2027. Major customers Emirates and Lufthansa forced to extend legacy 777-300ER and A380 service lives.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: THY'nin geniş gövde siparişlerinde Airbus A350-1000'e ağırlık vermesinde 777X gecikmeleri belirleyici stratejik etken oldu.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Delays were a primary catalyst for Turkish Airlines' decision to anchor its high-capacity widebody order book on the Airbus A350-1000.
programs.timeline_horizon: FAA tip sertifikasyonu ve ilk ticari teslimat 2026 sonu / 2027 hedefleniyor.
programs.source_reference: Boeing Defense, Space & Security / Airline IR Filings / Emirates President Statements

programs.title_tr: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Yüksek Basınç Türbini Dayanıklılığı & MRO Bekleme Süreleri
programs.title_en: CFM LEAP-1A / 1B Hot-Section Durability & Shop Visit Backlogs
programs.current_status_tr: Sıcak iklim, tozlu hava sahası ve yüksek iniş-kalkış döngüsü altında çalışan LEAP motorlarında türbin kanatçığı erozyonu nedeniyle planlanandan erken motor indirme yaşanıyor. Küresel MRO atölyelerinde yedek parça ve motor kıtlığı devam ediyor.
programs.current_status_en: Harsh environment operations (heat, sand, high cycle utilization) causing premature hot-section turbine blade wear; global MRO shops experiencing parts constraints and extended turn-around times.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_tr: Pegasus'un filosunun belkemiğini oluşturan A321neo uçaklarında CFM LEAP-1A motorları kullanılıyor. Pegasus, proaktif motor rotasyonu ve yedek motor rezervasyonu ile uçak yerde kalma süresini (AOG) asgaride tutuyor.
programs.thy_pegasus_impact_en: Pegasus relies heavily on CFM LEAP-1A on its A321neo fleet; carrier leverages proactive engine rotation and buffer lease pools to keep AOG rates minimal.
programs.timeline_horizon: CFM'in güncellenmiş dayanıklı parça (durability kit) teslimatları 2026 boyunca yaygınlaşıyor.
programs.source_reference: Safran / GE Aerospace Engine Technical Briefings / Aviation Week MRO Watch

stories.headline: European Aviation Network Traffic Drops 2.3% Week-on-Week Amid Weather Disruptions
stories.lead: European flight volumes fell to an average of 32,480 daily flights due to adverse weather and reduced capacity across major operators. Despite the weekly dip, overall network traffic remained 0.7% higher than the corresponding week in 2025.
stories.source_description: The network averaged 32,480 daily flights (including overflights), down 2.3% from Week 42 and 0.7% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Storms Austen and Boelo caused widespread flight disruptions across northern and western Europe between 23-25 October 2026. Among the 10 busiest carriers, capacity declined by an average of 1.3% week-on-week. Pegasus was the only carrier to record growth (+1%), while the KLM Group registered the largest decrease (-4%). Flight volumes across the 10 busiest States fell by an average of 2.5% with none recording growth. Greece saw the most significant decrease (-7%). Network arrival and departure punctuality were 73.5% and 69.4%, better than in the equivalent week of 2025. En-route ATFM delays decreased by 12% compared to the previous week, with a daily average of circa 54K delay minutes, and were 6% above 2025 levels. Total air traffic flow management (ATFM) delay was 2.4 min/flight (1.7 for en-route and 0.7 for airport). ATC capacity & staffing was the top delay cause (65% of all en-route ATFM delays), followed by weather (20%).

stories.headline: London Heathrow Retains Top Spot in OAG Megahubs 2025 Connectivity Rankings
stories.lead: London Heathrow retained its title as the world's most connected airport for the third consecutive year in the OAG Megahubs 2025 ranking. Meanwhile, Istanbul Airport and Frankfurt registered substantial connectivity gains, while Tokyo Haneda experienced a decline.
stories.source_description: London Heathrow (LHR) retains its title as the world’s most connected airport for the third consecutive year , offering over 59,000 possible connections to 226 destinations* on the busiest day**. Istanbul Airport (IST) has seen one of the greatest increases, surging from 8 th position last year to 2 nd place in this year’s ranking, due to a 25% year-on-year increase in potential connections on the busiest day of the year. Frankfurt (FRA) has seen a significant shift in rankings, climbing from 10 th position last year to 4 th , driven by a 21% increase in potential connections year-on-year. Tokyo Haneda (HND) has dropped down in this year’s rankings from 3 rd in 2024 to 9 th in 2025, reflecting a 10% decline in connections. Atlanta Hartsfield-Jackson (ATL) – the world’s largest airport by seat capacity – re-enters the Top 10 this year rising from 11 th place last year to 8 th position in 2025. ATL has added eight (8) more destinations and seen a corresponding 14% increase in potential connections. Chicago O’Hare (ORD) also makes gains, climbing two (2) spots to 7th, due to a 17% growth in connections and an expanded network of 15 additional destinations.
detailed_analysis: London Heathrow (LHR) offers over 59,000 possible connections to 226 destinations on its busiest day to hold 1st place for the third consecutive year.
Istanbul Airport (IST) climbed from 8th position last year to 2nd place following a 25% year-on-year increase in potential connections on its busiest day.
Frankfurt (FRA) rose from 10th position last year to 4th place, supported by a 21% year-on-year increase in potential connections.
Tokyo Haneda (HND) fell from 3rd place in 2024 to 9th place in 2025, reflecting a 10% decline in connections.

stories.headline: Emirates Opens USD 8 Million Centre of Hospitality Excellence to UAE Businesses
stories.lead: Emirates has opened its USD 8 million Centre of Hospitality Excellence in Dubai to external UAE businesses and brands for corporate upskilling. Located within the Emirates Crew Training Centre, the facility features presentation kitchens, classrooms, and a 170-guest lounge.
stories.source_description: Dubai, UAE, 9 November 2026: Emirates has now opened its world-class Centre of Hospitality Excellence in Dubai to UAE brands and businesses seeking to elevate hospitality culture and upskill their teams. An array of tailored and bespoke courses with interactive team-building sessions are now available to UAE companies and can be booked by contacting the dedicated email address*. Located within the Emirates Crew Training Centre, the USD 8 million Centre of Hospitality Excellence offers a premium learning environment inspired by the airline’s globally recognised hospitality philosophy. The purpose-built space features a restaurant and lounge accommodating up to 170 guests, elegant presentation kitchens, and eight technology-enabled classrooms designed to deliver immersive hospitality training experiences. Modelled on the standards that shape Emirates’ award-winning inflight customer experience, the Centre of Hospitality Excellence offers organisations the opportunity to learn directly from the airline’s expertise in delivering refined, personalised hospitality at scale. The centre delivers programmes inspired by Michelin-star hospitality principles, covering fine dining protocols, guest engagement, service etiquette and leadership in customer experience. Since launching its external programmes, the centre has already welcomed a range of organisations including government entities, leading universities and major regional companies seeking to strengthen hospitality culture across their teams. Divisional Senior Vice President Service Delivery, Emirates, Thomas Ney said; ‘Delivering exceptional hospitality requires more than technical training, it demands a deep understanding of people, culture and service excellence. At Emirates, we have spent decades refining our approach to hospitality through continuous learning and innovation, delivered to millions of global customers. By opening the Centre of Hospitality Excellence to organisations across the UAE, we are proud to share this expertise and help inspire the next generation of hospitality professionals.’ Hospitality training programmes available for UAE businesses A range of immersive workshops and experiences can be tailored to individual organisation’s needs and arranged over 1-5 days of training - designed to strengthen hospitality culture and enhance customer experience. Organisations can select modules and workshops that are the most relevant to their training objectives. Topics include: Hospitality Excellence - A tailored workshop designed to introduce Emirates’ House of Hospitality while addressing each organisation’s unique development needs. The programme begins with a training gap analysis and incorporates interactive exercises, case studies and practical activities to create an engaging learning environment. 7-Star Dining Experience - Focused on the art of refined dining, this programme explores table settings, etiquette, presentation and guest interaction. Participants develop a deeper understanding of how attention to detail and anticipation of guest needs contribute to exceptional hospitality. L’Art du Vin - Delivered by WSET Level 3-certified wine trainers, this programme builds on Emirates’ successful wine education training for cabin crew. Participants explore wine theory, tasting techniques and food pairing, with optional guided tasting experiences designed to deepen practical understanding. Gastronomy - Led by a team of chefs with experience spanning global kitchens, this hands-on workshop introduces participants to advanced culinary techniques, flavour profiling and plating artistry while exploring the philosophy behind world-class gastronomy. Team-building experiences – Designed on a bespoke basis, Emirates Centre of Hospitality Excellence creates interactive challenges and culinary activities designed to encourage collaboration, strengthen communication and build strong team dynamics. Leadership at Emirates – Conference and thought leadership sessions are available featuring Emirates executives who share insights into the airline’s global operations, leadership approach and service strategy. Behind-the-scenes tours - Participants gain access to Emirates’ advanced training facilities, including aircraft simulators and culinary training hubs, offering a rare look at how world-class hospitality is delivered at scale. Tours/Experiences can also be enhanced with catering experiences, as well as professional photography and videography. Bespoke hospitality programmes - In addition to structured workshops, the Centre of Hospitality Excellence offers customised learning experiences designed to meet the specific objectives of organisations. These bespoke programmes combine training sessions, culinary demonstrations, leadership discussions, interactive service challenges, learner assessments and immersive dining experiences to create comprehensive learning journeys tailored to each organisation’s operational environment. Emirates’ investment in world-class hospitality and training The Centre of Hospitality Excellence forms part of Emirates’ continued investment in service innovation and hospitality training. In 2020, Emirates partnered with one of the world’s leading hospitality management schools, Ecole hôtelière de Lausanne in Switzerland to develop an elevated hospitality strategy for the airline. The collaboration helped shape Emirates’ customer experience philosophy, which is built around four pillars: excellence, attentiveness, innovation and passion. Today, the Centre of Hospitality Excellence stands as a flagship embodiment of this strategy, helping to inspire both Emirates employees and external organisations to deliver exceptional hospitality experiences. The facility is also an integral part of Emirates’ cabin crew training ecosystem. Emirates currently employs 25,000+ cabin crew recruited from more than 140 nationalities and speaking over 70 languages. All Emirates’ cabin crew undergo training at the Emirates Crew Training Centre in Dubai, completing an intensive eight-week programme covering safety and emergency procedures, aviation security, medical training, hospitality, service delivery and image & uniform standards. Training combines classroom learning with practical simulations, including full-motion aircraft simulators representing Emirates’ fleet. Throughout their careers, cabin crew continue to receive intensive training as they are promoted through cabins and into leadership roles. Within the Centre of Hospitality Excellence, cabin crew also participate in immersive dining sessions where they experience service from the guest perspective. During these sessions, crew enjoy a curated four-course gastronomy lunch prepared by Emirates’ master chefs and featuring some of the airline’s most celebrated First and Business Class dishes. The experience allows them to observe best-practice service delivered by Emirates’ training team while deepening their understanding of guest expectations. The centre’s Culinary Hub also features a purpose-built training kitchen designed as a fusion between a professional restaurant kitchen and an aircraft galley, where cabin crew learn the art of plating from experienced chef trainers, mastering the balance of colour, texture and presentation. In addition, the centre hosts wine tastings and specialist sessions led by expert sommeliers and wine trainers as part of Emirates’ L’Art du Vin learning programme.
